_source: Promoted from the phase-0 lab corners `.scratch/explain-lab-q13-corners.ts` (Q13, #185), all 22 of which pass unchanged against the shipped module — the ratified expectations, each carrying the device probe or corpus file it was read off. C1-C22 are those corners. F1a-F2d are the branch anchors for the two behaviors promoted BEYOND the lab SUT (substitution-in-string, closure scope); they were device-verified on CHR 7.23.2 before being frozen here, so no fixture in this file is hand-asserted. X1-X6 are behavior anchors for surfaces the oracle cannot express (empty input, structural notes, scan resumption). `cls: null` is an ABSTENTION and a first-class expected outcome: Q13's central finding is that offline may say what a name is bound to and must never say that a bare word is unbound.

cases.name: S1 :local declares and its use resolves
cases.rule: S1/S4 — probe `local-variable` @7.23.2 pairs: both occurrences `variable-local`

cases.name: S2 :global declares and its use resolves
cases.rule: S2/S4 — probe `global-variable` @7.23.2

cases.name: S3 :foreach binds its loop variable as auto
cases.rule: S3 — probe `foreach-counter` @7.23.2: `variable-auto` at declaration and use

cases.name: S6 positional parameters are `parameter`
cases.rule: S6 — probe `function-parameter` @7.23.2

cases.name: S5 an undeclared $name is `parameter`, NOT an error
cases.rule: S5 — probe `undefined-variable` @7.23.2. The console cannot distinguish 'undeclared' from 'supplied at call time', so `parameter` is the CORRECT answer, not a fallback. An offline resolver that flagged this as an error would be wrong.

cases.name: S1 a local does NOT escape the function body that declared it
cases.rule: S1 scope extent — grounded on test.rsc @pre-7.23: `vlanid` is `variable-local` inside the `pvid2array` body (offsets 959–2420) and `variable-parameter` from the `mkvlan` body onward (4231+). The device treats the second function's reference as a call-time parameter. This is the fixture that caught the reference-scan depth drift: `$v]`/`$v)` swallowed their closing bracket, nesting never unwound, and locals leaked across every function in the file.

cases.name: S1 an inner :local shadows an outer one
cases.rule: S4 — nearest-enclosing wins. Both resolve to `local`, so the CLASS is stable under shadowing; only the binding identity changes, which highlight cannot observe (it emits a class, not a symbol id). Recorded so the limit is explicit: this corner is class-invisible to the oracle.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 highlight: all four `v` occurrences = `variable-local` — the CLASS is stable under shadowing (device-confirmed); the binding-identity claim remains inherently unobservable by highlight, as recorded.

cases.name: S2 a global stays visible inside a nested block
cases.rule: S2 — globals are recorded at depth 0 and survive brace exit

cases.name: S11 a QUOTED declaration name
cases.rule: S11 — grounded on test.rsc: the device classes `"set-dns"` `variable-global` INCLUDING the quotes. Without this rule the string is skipped and the next bare word (`do`) is declared instead — which is what the first Q13 run did.

cases.name: S18 :onerror binds its error variable
cases.rule: S18 — grounded on eworm/backup-cloud.rsc: `:onerror Err {…} do={… $Err}` and the device's class set contains no `variable-parameter`. Q2 established the same head-directive slot for block naming.

cases.name: S10 :set is a reference, not a declaration
cases.rule: S10 — grounded on test.rsc: the `:set` target carries the class it was DECLARED as. `:set` never introduces a binding; on an undeclared name the device emits a hard `error` (highlight-format.md §4), so the resolver abstains there instead of inventing a class.

cases.name: S10 :set on an undeclared name abstains
cases.rule: S10 — the device's answer is a hard `error`, which is not a variable class at all. Abstaining is the only honest offline output.

cases.name: S14 `->` terminates a reference name
cases.rule: S14 — grounded on test.rsc: the device classes `vlanbytes` `variable-local` and `->0` separately. A greedy `-`-inclusive scan yields `vlanbytes-`, fails lookup, and degrades to `parameter`.

cases.name: S14 `.` terminates a reference name
cases.rule: S14 — grounded on test.rsc. The dotted `arg-scope`/`arg-dot` form is for ARGUMENT names, not variables (highlight-format.md §3.1).

cases.name: S19 `-` inside a name vs `-` as an operator
cases.rule: S19 — `-` is legal inside a name (`set-dns`) AND is the operator. The document's own declarations break the tie: the full run `octive-1` does not resolve, the prefix `octive` does. Same longest-resolving-prefix move Q0 rev 3 used for fused `path+arg` slugs.

cases.name: S8 a menu field in a filter region is schema-dependent — abstain
cases.rule: S8 — the console binds the target menu's fields as locals, so a real field is `variable-local` and a typo is `variable-undefined`. Telling them apart needs the menu schema; offline abstains.

cases.name: S8 bare field references in a query expression also abstain
cases.rule: S8 widened — grounded on eworm/check-certificates.rsc. The `field=value` form is not the only one: bare field names in a query expression are menu fields too. `or` is an operator (S17), not a symbol.

cases.name: S7 REVISED — a bare word in expression position is never asserted
cases.rule: S7 — asserting `variable-undefined` here measured 2.5% precision on the holdout (39 false positives vs 1 true positive). A bare word in expression position is far more often a menu field or a query flag than a genuine unresolved name. Abstention is the pre-registered response to that, and it is the same conclusion Q3 reached for absolute inner paths.

cases.name: S12 a sigilled word is a directive or path segment, never a symbol
cases.rule: S12 — `:typeof` is `cmd` on the device; only `$x` is a symbol. The sigil is the schema-free tell.

cases.name: S16 space-separated menu path segments are not symbols
cases.rule: S16 — grounded on test.rsc: `list` is `dir` on the device. The space-separated path form (Q3/R4) leaves later segments without a `/` sigil, so the sigil rule alone reads `list` as an identifier. `LAN` is a VALUE after `=` (S15), classified `none`.

cases.name: S13 bare literals are values, not symbols
cases.rule: S13 — grounded on test.rsc: `true` is `none` on the device.

cases.name: S9 a reference inside a double-quoted string still resolves
cases.rule: S9 — grounded on test.rsc: `$vlanid` inside a `:put "…"` string carries its scope class (offsets 2475/2746 are `variable-local`). String interpolation does NOT reset scope resolution — a hypothesis the scoring explicitly refuted before the real cause (scope extent) was found.

cases.name: a `$[…]` substitution carrying a nested string does not break later bindings
cases.rule: F1 — the substitution is CODE, so its nested string closes inside it. A scan that reads it as string bytes flips its quote phase here and every later binding is lost (the lab SUT read both `pos` uses as `parameter`).
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a `#` line after such a substitution is a comment, not string content
cases.rule: F1 — H4 must be decided by a scanner that models substitutions. `segment.ts`'s shared `maskComments` does not, so it leaves this comment unmasked; the device classes the whole `# :put $a` line `comment`.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a named-function body is a closure: the outer local reads parameter
cases.rule: F2 — the console cannot see the enclosing binding from inside a function definition, so it falls back to `parameter` (S5). The lab SUT, being depth-scoped, said `local`.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a control-flow do={} body SHARES the enclosing scope
cases.rule: F2 — the contrast case. `:if`/`:foreach`/`:while`/`:do` bodies are not closures, and they spell `do={` exactly like a function definition; the statement head is the only tell.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a global needs an in-body `:global` re-import inside a function
cases.rule: F2 — the eworm idiom, device-confirmed: the re-imported `$G` reads `global`, the one in the body without a re-import reads `parameter`.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a loop variable is visible in the loop body but not through a function
cases.rule: F2 + S3 — `auto` bindings obey the same closure boundary as locals.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a colon-less `onerror` binds its error variable exactly like `:onerror`
cases.rule: S18 + Q2's colon-optional finding (`do {` opens a body the same way `:do {` does), which `blocks.ts` already encodes in DIRECTIVE_BODY. Unlike `:local`/`:global`/`:set`, the error-variable head is deliberately NOT gated on the `:` sigil.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight` (2026-08-02): `onerror Err {…} do={… $Err}` and `:onerror Err {…} do={… $Err}` produce byte-identical classes, `Err` = `variable-local` in both. Same for the `in={…} do={…}` spelling.

cases.name: an escaped newline continues the statement, so the declaration survives
cases.rule: F4 (Q1 H5) — a `\` at end of line is a continuation, not a boundary. Resetting statement state here dropped the declaration and then reported `$foo` as a confident `parameter`; the device says `variable-local` at both occurrences.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: an escaped newline before `do={` keeps the body a closure
cases.rule: F4 + F2 — the continuation must also carry `declaredHere`, or the function body stops being a closure and the outer local leaks into it. Device: the in-body `outer` is `variable-parameter`.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a colon-less `local` head declares
cases.rule: F3 — the sigil is optional; requiring `:` skipped the declaration and made every later use a confident `parameter`.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a colon-less `global` head declares
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a colon-less `foreach` head binds its loop variable
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a colon-less `for` head binds its loop variable
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a colon-less `set` targets an existing binding
cases.rule: F3 + S10 — the device reports all three occurrences `variable-local`.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a colon-less `set` on an unknown name is the MENU verb — no variable
cases.rule: F3 + S10 — spelling decides: bare `set` with nothing in scope is the menu verb and the device reports NO variable, while `:set`/`/set` are the scripting command and report a hard `error`, so those abstain instead (C12).
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a root-path head is the scripting command; a deeper path is a menu item
cases.rule: F3 — `/local` at ROOT is the scripting command and binds (device: `foo` = `variable-local`). Contrast `/ip/local foo 1` and `/interface local foo 1`, where the device makes `local` an `obj-inactive` menu item and `foo` `none`; there the head word is `ip`/`interface`, so no declaration is made either.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a head word is only a head at STATEMENT START
cases.rule: F3 boundary — `head === null` is not the statement-start test, because nothing before a bare word sets it. Device: `local` and the first `foo` are `none` (no declaration is made) and the later `$foo` is `variable-parameter`. Reading `local` as a head here fabricated a binding and then reported that `$foo` as a confident `local`.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a word after a bracket is not a head either
cases.rule: F3 boundary — same rule, second shape. Device: `local`/`foo` `none`, `$x` and the later `$foo` `variable-parameter`.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a doubled sigil is not a scripting head
cases.rule: F3 boundary — the sigil run must be zero or one character. Device: `//local foo 1` is an error and EVERY byte of the document reads `none`, so no declaration may be made. The trailing `$foo` reading is plain S5 on input the console rejects outright, not a claim about a binding.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a malformed escape stops the analysis
cases.rule: F4 — in code a backslash is valid only before whitespace. Device: the doubled backslash errors on the FIRST one, `foo` is `none`, and nothing after is a variable. The resolver records `bad-escape:<offset>` and reports nothing further rather than continuing across a boundary the console never crossed.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: a malformed escape cannot fabricate a closure
cases.rule: F4 + F2 — `do=\{` is not `do={`. Device: `outer` and `fn` are `variable-local`, then the error kills the rest (`put` and the in-body `outer` read `none`). Occurrences before the defect stand (the lab's X1 rule); the body is never entered.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: an escaped space is a valid escape, not a defect
cases.rule: F4 — CHR 7.23.2 accepts `\ ` and `\<tab>` in code with no error and still classes `$v` `variable-local`; only a backslash before a NON-whitespace character is malformed.
cases.verified: CHR 7.23.2 `/console/inspect request=highlight`, probe `.scratch/q13-anchor-chr-probe.ts` (2026-08-02): every occurrence below carries the device class shown, and the device reported no variable the resolver missed.

cases.name: empty input resolves to nothing
cases.rule: Never throws, reports nothing, notes nothing.

cases.name: a comments-only document has no symbols
cases.rule: S9 — a reference inside a comment is not classified.

cases.name: an unterminated string is reported, not thrown
cases.rule: Structural notes use the segmenter's vocabulary; classes are still reported for what was read.

cases.name: a stray close is reported
cases.rule: `unbalanced-close:<char>` — same vocabulary as `segment.ts`.

cases.name: an unclosed scope is reported
cases.rule: `unclosed:<chars>` lists the delimiters still open at end of input.

cases.name: a `$name` stops ON its terminator, so nesting stays balanced
cases.rule: The `next` vs `end` distinction in `readRef`: the lab's first run consumed the `]` here and drifted depth upward across the rest of the document.
